examples.ko: 길에서 차가 고장 나서 견인차를 불렀어요.
examples.en: My car broke down on the road, so I called a tow truck.

examples.ko: 견인차가 우리 차를 정비소로 끌고 갔어요.
examples.en: The tow truck pulled our car to the repair shop.
I parked illegally and my car was towed.
They say the tow truck driver will arrive soon.

examples.ko: 사고 현장에 견인차 두 대가 왔어요.
examples.en: Two tow trucks came to the scene of the accident.
The towing cost was more expensive than I thought, which surprised me.

explain: 견인차는 고장 난 차나 불법 주차한 차를 끌고 가는 차예요. 보험을 쓰면 '긴급 출동'이라는 서비스로 부르기도 해요. 입말에서는 '레커차'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: A tow truck came and took the car away.
phrases.nuance_en: A spoken word used in place of 견인차.

phrases.en: The tow truck came thirty minutes later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도움을 요청한 뒤 차가 도착할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the truck arrives after you asked for help.

phrases.example: 불법 주차해서 제 차가 견인차에 끌려갔어요.
phrases.en: I parked illegally, so my car was towed away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차가 허락 없이 옮겨졌을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a car has been moved away without permission.

explain_en: A 견인차 tows away broken-down or illegally parked cars. With car insurance you can often call one as an '긴급 출동' (emergency dispatch) service. In casual speech it is also called '레커차'.

examples.en: If you cross the overpass, the subway station is right there.

examples.ko: 이 구름다리는 큰 도로 위에 있어요.
examples.en: This overpass is above a big road.
The night view from the overpass is wonderful.
I held my child's hand and crossed the overpass.
A new overpass was built between the parks.
The overpass stairs are high, so it's tiring.

explain: 도로나 철길 위로 사람이 걸어서 건너는 높은 다리예요. '육교'라고도 해요. 건물과 건물 사이를 잇는 다리를 말할 때도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I cross the overpass and go to the bus stop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 말이고, 도로 위를 건너는 다리는 일상에서 '육교'라고 더 많이 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning; for a bridge over a road, 육교 is the more common everyday word.

phrases.en: I looked down at the road from the overpass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다리 위에 있는 장소를 말할 때 '위'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 위 (on top) to talk about standing on the bridge.

phrases.en: The two buildings are connected by a bridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물과 건물 사이를 잇는 다리를 말할 때 이렇게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for a bridge linking two buildings.

explain_en: It is an elevated bridge people walk across over a road or railway, also called '육교'. It can also describe a bridge connecting two buildings.

examples.en: The children just stood far off and watched.
I parked the car far away and walked.
I was scared of the dog, so I went around at a distance.

examples.ko: 멀찌감치 떨어져서 보면 그림이 더 잘 보여요.
examples.en: If you stand far back, you can see the painting better.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 나를 보고 멀찌감치 피해 갔어요.
examples.en: That person saw me and steered clear at a distance.
Drive keeping a good distance from the car ahead.

explain: 꽤 멀리 떨어져 있는 모양을 나타내요. 그냥 '멀리'보다 일부러 거리를 두거나 떨어져 있는 상황에 잘 어울려요. '멀찍이'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.en: I watched from a good distance away.
phrases.nuance_ko: '멀찌감치'와 같은 뜻이고 조금 더 짧게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 'meoljjigamchi', just a little shorter.

phrases.en: I was scared of the dog, so I moved far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 거리를 두고 물러날 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for deliberately keeping your distance.

phrases.nuance_ko: '멀찌감치'보다 일반적이고 일부러 거리를 두는 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More general than 'meoljjigamchi', with less sense of keeping distance on purpose.

explain_en: It describes being quite far away. Compared with plain '멀리', it fits well when someone keeps their distance on purpose. '멀찍이' is used with the same meaning.

examples.en: The main road was blocked, so we went around by a side road.
Walking along the path through the forest is refreshing.

examples.ko: 지름길인 줄 알았는데 샛길이 막혀 있었어요.
examples.en: I thought it was a shortcut, but the side road was blocked.
Cars can't enter this side road.
The child was playing on a side path and got lost.

examples.ko: 논 사이의 샛길을 지나 건널목에 이르렀어요.
examples.en: We passed along a path between the rice fields and reached the crossing.

explain: 큰길에서 갈라져 나온 작은 길이에요. 빠르게 가는 '지름길'과는 달리, 단지 크기가 작은 길이라 돌아가거나 한적한 곳을 걸을 때 써요. 이야기나 행동이 본래 방향에서 벗어날 때 비유로도 써요.

phrases.en: The story went off on a tangent and I forgot the main point.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이나 행동이 중심에서 벗어나 다른 쪽으로 흘러간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means that speech or behavior drifts away from the main point.

explain_en: It is a small path that branches off from a main road. Unlike '지름길' (a shortcut that is faster), it simply means a small road, so it is used for detours or quiet walks. It is also used figuratively when a story or action drifts away from the main direction.

examples.en: The captain sat in the cockpit and checked the plane.

examples.ko: 조종석 문은 비행 중에 잠겨 있어요.
examples.en: The cockpit door stays locked during the flight.

examples.ko: 아이는 장난감 비행기의 조종석을 신기하게 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: The child gazed in wonder at the cockpit of the toy plane.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 실제 전투기 조종석에 앉아 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: At the museum, you can sit in the cockpit of a real fighter jet.
What does the sky look like from the cockpit?
A helicopter cockpit is narrower than you'd think.

explain: '조종석'은 비행기, 헬리콥터, 우주선처럼 조종하는 사람이 앉는 자리예요. 자동차, 버스, 택시는 '운전석'이라고 하니까 '조종'과 '운전'을 구분해 보세요. 배는 '조타실'이라는 말을 써요.

phrases.example: 아이가 조종석에 앉아 보고 싶어 해요.
phrases.en: The child wants to sit in the cockpit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자리에 앉는다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for sitting in the seat.

phrases.en: I could see clouds through the cockpit window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조종석 안이나 주변에 있는 것을 말할 때 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before a noun to talk about things in or around the cockpit.

phrases.en: A helicopter cockpit is very narrow.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the type of vehicle in front.

explain_en: 조종석 is the seat where the pilot sits in a plane, helicopter, or spaceship. For cars, buses, and taxis, Koreans say 운전석 instead, so keep 조종 and 운전 apart. For a ship's wheelhouse, the word is 조타실.

examples.en: A new paved road has been built to the village.
Even when it rains, paved roads are easy to walk on.
We went through the mountain path and came out onto a paved road.
From where the paved road ends, it's a dirt road.

examples.ko: 이 길은 포장도로라서 자전거 타기 좋아요.
examples.en: This is a paved road, so it's good for cycling.
In winter the paved road froze and was slippery.

explain: 아스팔트나 시멘트로 단단하게 깔아 놓은 길이에요. 반대는 흙길이나 '비포장도로'예요. '비포장도로'는 차가 흔들려서 운전이 힘들다고 말할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 새 포장도로를 달리니까 차가 안 흔들려요.
phrases.en: The car doesn't shake on the new paved road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차가 달리는 길을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the road a car drives on.
phrases.en_equiv: to drive on a paved road

phrases.en: The dirt road became a paved road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길이 달라진 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a road that has been changed.

phrases.en: It's a paved path, so it's good for cycling.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple everyday way to say the same thing.

explain_en: It is a road laid firmly with asphalt or cement. The opposite is a dirt road, or '비포장도로'. '비포장도로' often comes up when saying the car shakes and driving is hard.

examples.en: I want to build a mud house in the countryside and live there.
That mud house was quite cool even in summer.

examples.ko: 산골에 있는 작은 흙집에서 하룻밤 잤어요.
examples.en: I stayed one night in a small mud house in the mountains.
I went to a mud-house experience village with the kids.

examples.ko: 마을 끝에 낡은 흙집이 한 채 남아 있어요.
examples.en: One old mud house remains at the end of the village.
It's a café with a cozy feel like a mud house.

explain: 흙으로 지은 집을 말해요. 황토로 지은 집은 '황토집'이라고도 하는데, 건강과 자연 이야기를 할 때 자주 나와요. 지붕 재료로 이름 붙인 '초가집'과는 기준이 달라요.

phrases.en: A yellow-clay house is warm in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 황토로 지은 흙집을 말하고, 건강한 집이라는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A mud house made of yellow clay, with a healthy-living feel.

phrases.en: My friend built a mud house by himself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 만든다고 할 때 '짓다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '짓다' when saying someone builds a house.

phrases.en: My grandfather lived in a mud house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사는 곳을 말할 때 조사 '에서'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the particle '에서' when talking about where someone lives.
phrases.en_equiv: to live in a mud house

explain_en: It means a house built of earth. A house built of ocher clay is also called '황토집', which often comes up in talk about health and nature. It differs from '초가집', which is named for its thatched roof.
